newsitem.title: USA: Texas hospital settles IRS charges on bond status.
newsitem.headline: Texas hospital settles IRS charges on bond status.

text.p: A Texas hospital announced Tuesday that it settled Internal Revenue Service charges concerning the tax-exempt status of millions of dollars in revenue bonds.

Monty Humble, attorney for Methodist Hospital of Lubbock, would not say how much the hospital paid to settle IRS charges that it may have abridged its status as a so-called 501(c)(3) issuer because of some long-term lease agreements with a local physician group and other issues.
But Humble, a partner with Vinson & Elkins in Dallas, said the total figure was at least 10 percent of the institution's annual net profits.

"The Service is increasing the price of settlements," Humble said. Asked by how much, Humble said "noticeably." He said the hospital's violations were less aggregious than those of other medical facilities that ended up paying the same amount.
On the other hand, Humble said, "It seems to indicate that the Service favors settlement versus declaring the bonds taxable. I think it will be a relief to the market."
Humble said the hospital retains its status as a 501(c)(3) organization under the pact with IRS.
The agreement clears the way for the hospital's proposed merger with St. Mary of Plains Hospital and Rehabilitation Center, also in Lubbock, he added.
